item.text:
Researched 7B only. No score returned.

**Reused Evidence**
- `E0001` is reused as authority and attribution context only, not as proof of integrity conduct. `REUSE_JSON: {"evidence_ids":["E0001"],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.6"]}`

**New Evidence**
- `Khamenei Blames Protests on West` by The Iran Primer, USIP, 2022-06-08, https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2022/jun/08/khamenei-blames-protests-west. Khamenei framed the June 2022 protests as enemy-driven, invoked social media and hired mercenaries, and told Iranians not to accept that the country had reached a dead end. That is direct ruler speech and strong evidence for a repeated blame-shift pattern, though it could still reflect sincere belief rather than provable knowing deception. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Khamenei Blames Protests on West","publisher":"The Iran Primer, USIP","publication_date":"2022-06-08","url":"https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2022/jun/08/khamenei-blames-protests-west","claim":"Khamenei framed the June 2022 protests as enemy-driven manipulation, using social media, psychological warfare, and mercenaries, and urged Iranians not to believe the country had reached a dead end.","locator":"lines 25-30, 45-47, 66-70","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct quotation of a 2022 speech in a reputable policy source, but still secondhand and interpretive.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct target-year speech during the 2022 protest cycle.","ruler_attribution":"Direct personal speech by Khamenei.","contrary_evidence":["Could reflect a genuinely held regime belief rather than conscious deception.","The source is a summary of the speech, not the full official transcript."],"lenses":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"]}`
- `Iran's supreme leader blames protests on Israel and US` by Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 2022-10-03, https://www.jta.org/2022/10/03/global/irans-supreme-leader-blames-protests-on-israel-and-us. Khamenei publicly blamed the unrest on U.S. and Israeli schemes and, as reported, offered no evidence for that claim. This is direct personal rhetoric and strong 7B evidence for blame-shifting and public misrepresentation, though it does not by itself prove intent. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran's supreme leader blames protests on Israel and US","publisher":"Jewish Telegraphic Agency","publication_date":"2022-10-03","url":"https://www.jta.org/2022/10/03/global/irans-supreme-leader-blames-protests-on-israel-and-us","claim":"Khamenei publicly blamed the 2022 unrest on U.S. and Israeli schemes and did not provide evidence for that accusation.","locator":"lines 71-74","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Directly quotes a Reuters-sourced speech with explicit note that no evidence was offered.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct target-year speech during the Mahsa Amini protest wave.","ruler_attribution":"Direct personal speech by Khamenei.","contrary_evidence":["Could still be sincere propaganda rather than knowingly false belief.","The article reports the absence of evidence, but absence of evidence is not absolute proof of deception."],"lenses":["7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"]}`
- `Iran’s supreme leader built a real estate empire on seized property` by Quartz, 2022-07-21, https://qz.com/146187/irans-supreme-leader-built-a-real-estate-empire-on-seized-property. The Reuters investigation summarized here says Khamenei controlled a roughly $95 billion Setad network built partly from confiscated property, that parliament had barred oversight over his business interests, and that the structure gave him economic clout and independence from the elected government. Reuters also said it found no evidence that he personally tapped the assets to enrich himself, so the strongest claim is office power and network benefit, not proven personal pocketing. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran’s supreme leader built a real estate empire on seized property","publisher":"Quartz","publication_date":"2022-07-21","url":"https://qz.com/146187/irans-supreme-leader-built-a-real-estate-empire-on-seized-property","claim":"A Reuters investigation reported that Khamenei controlled a roughly $95 billion Setad network built partly on confiscated property, with parliamentary oversight barred over his business interests, while Reuters found no evidence he personally used the assets to enrich himself.","locator":"lines 91-116","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Secondary summary of a Reuters investigation with concrete asset and governance claims, but still not the primary Reuters page.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"2022 publication describing a standing structure that existed in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct to Khamenei through control of Setad and the Supreme Leader’s office; no proof of personal cash enrichment.","contrary_evidence":["Reuters said it found no evidence that Khamenei personally tapped Setad to enrich himself.","The underlying asset structure is long-running rather than a single 2022 act."],"lenses":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"]}`
- `Fact Check: Are Ali Khamenei's Living Standards 'Below Average'?` by IranWire, 2022-04-19, https://prod.iranwire.com/en/khameneicom/103191-fact-check-are-ali-khameneis-living-standards-below-average/. IranWire treated the chief of staff’s “below average” austerity claim as misleading and said Khamenei’s exact assets are not public, which cuts against office messaging that tries to sanitize his material position. This is useful but indirect, because it is a fact-check of a staff claim, not a sworn statement or asset filing from Khamenei himself. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Fact Check: Are Ali Khamenei's Living Standards 'Below Average'?","publisher":"IranWire","publication_date":"2022-04-19","url":"https://prod.iranwire.com/en/khameneicom/103191-fact-check-are-ali-khameneis-living-standards-below-average/","claim":"IranWire said the chief of staff’s claim that Khamenei lived at below-average standards was misleading, while also noting that Khamenei’s exact assets were not publicly known.","locator":"search result excerpt / article text highlighted in snippet","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Fact-checking outlet with a focused claim, but the publicly accessible snippet does not provide a full forensic asset record.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Directly about a 2022 public claim concerning Khamenei’s personal lifestyle.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect via a chief-of-staff claim about Khamenei; not a direct personal statement from him.","contrary_evidence":["The article says exact assets are unknown, so it does not prove self-enrichment.","It checks a claimed lifestyle, not a formal disclosure or audited financial filing."],"lenses":["7B.2","7B.10"]}`
- `Iran protests highlight its crisis of legitimacy` by Chatham House, 2022-09-28, https://www.chathamhouse.org/2022/09/iran-protests-highlight-its-crisis-legitimacy. Chatham House describes Khamenei’s office as vetting key ministers and ambassadors, and says the deep state includes the judiciary, parastatal foundations, and the Supreme Leader’s office, with IRGC intelligence embedded there. That is strong context for appointment control, scrutiny limitation, and patronage networks, but it is still structural evidence rather than a single 2022 act of personal dishonesty. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Iran protests highlight its crisis of legitimacy","publisher":"Chatham House","publication_date":"2022-09-28","url":"https://www.chathamhouse.org/2022/09/iran-protests-highlight-its-crisis-legitimacy","claim":"Chatham House said Khamenei’s office vetted key ministers and ambassadors, and that the deep state, including the Supreme Leader’s office and IRGC intelligence, had detailed oversight over Iranian political processes.","locator":"lines 439-445 and 453-464","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reputable policy analysis with clear lines tying office structure to power and vetting, though it is still secondary analysis.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Published during the 2022 protest and succession crisis, describing structures operating in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Structural power under Khamenei, not a discrete personal act.","contrary_evidence":["The source is about regime structure more than a specific integrity episode.","It shows capacity and network, not direct proof of personal self-dealing in 2022."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.7","7B.9"]}`
- `Treasury Designates Supreme Leader of Iran’s Inner Circle Responsible for Advancing Regime’s Domestic and Foreign Oppression` by U.S. Department of the Treasury, 2019-11-04, https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm824. Treasury said Mojtaba Khamenei represented the Supreme Leader despite never being elected or appointed to government, and that Khamenei and his office directed the blocking of Baha’i social and economic progress. This is older than the target year, but it is a direct official finding about the Supreme Leader’s office and family network, so it is useful as persistent background on nepotism and office capture. `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Treasury Designates Supreme Leader of Iran’s Inner Circle Responsible for Advancing Regime’s Domestic and Foreign Oppression","publisher":"U.S. Department of the Treasury","publication_date":"2019-11-04","url":"https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sm824","claim":"Treasury said Mojtaba Khamenei represented the Supreme Leader without having been elected or appointed to government, and that Khamenei and his office directed the blocking of Baha'i social and economic progress.","locator":"lines 619-626","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary official sanctions finding with explicit attributions and names.","final_evidence_use":"context","period_fit":"Pre-2022 but describing a standing office pattern that remained relevant in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Strong attribution to Khamenei’s office and delegated family network; not a 2022 event, but a documented pattern.","contrary_evidence":["It is an adversarial sanctions finding, so the wording is prosecutorial rather than neutral.","It predates 2022, so it should be read as standing context rather than year-specific conduct."],"lenses":["7B.5","7B.7","7B.9"]}`

**Search And Rejection Summary**
- I reviewed roughly 30 documents across Reuters derivatives, official U.S. Treasury releases, Chatham House, USIP/Iran Primer, IranWire, JTA, Press TV, Tasnim, the U.S. State Department 2022 human-rights report, and several Iran-specific explainers and fact-checks.
- I kept only items with a direct Khamenei nexus, or a clearly persistent Supreme Leader office / family-network nexus that materially informs 2022 integrity judgments.
- I rejected or downgraded repeated protest-crackdown coverage from Reuters/Euronews, Press TV, Tasnim, Iran International, and similar items when they duplicated the same blame-shift quote or mostly belonged to 3B and 4B rather than 7B.
- I rejected generic country-level corruption, sanctions, economy, and protest materials unless they tied directly to Khamenei’s own statements, his office, Setad, or his family network.
- I rejected most 2022 internet-shutdown and protest-suppression articles as adjacent-chapter evidence, because they show repression but do not by themselves prove Khamenei’s personal dishonesty or self-dealing.
- I treated older materials as context only when they documented standing structures that plausibly persisted into 2022, rather than as year-specific acts.
- I did not use the client matrix.

**Remaining Gaps**
- There is still no direct 2022 financial disclosure, asset declaration, or audited record showing Khamenei’s personal wealth or gifts.
- I did not find a 2022 primary document proving Khamenei personally ordered concealment of his own financial affairs.
- Evidence on admissions of error, corrections, or truthful self-correction remains thin.
- The strongest negative evidence is speech-based and structural, not forensic on personal enrichment.
- More search would help mainly on Persian-language court filings, leaked office records, sanctions dossiers, and investigative reporting on the Supreme Leader’s office, family holdings, and any 2022-specific assets or appointments.
